title: Big Female Pythons Cause the Most Trouble in Florida
summary:
Burmese pythons are a big problem in Florida. These huge snakes are an invasive species, meaning they are not native there and can harm the local environment. Florida allows people to hunt them all year, and even holds a 10-day competition to catch as many as possible.

But scientists say a free-for-all approach may not be the best way to reduce the population, estimated at 100,000 to 300,000 snakes. In a study published in the journal Ecological Applications, conservationists argue that being more selective about targets could make a bigger difference.

Alex Romer, an ecologist with the University of Florida Croc Doc Wildlife Research Team, said earlier work treated all Burmese pythons as contributing equally to the population. He said removing the biggest female ever caught is very different from removing a tiny snake that might not survive next year.

Romer and his colleagues analyzed data from the South Florida Water Management District's Python Elimination Program. They developed a new system called the Weighted Removal Index, or WRI. Points are awarded to a snake depending on factors including its age, sex, and the time of year it was caught.

Younger snakes do not get a high index ranking because many die naturally before they can breed. For the largest impact, researchers suggest pursuing mature female pythons.

"Every Burmese python removed is a win for the Everglades, but targeting large reproductive females is likely to reduce the population most effectively," explained UF invasive ecologist Melissa Miller.

The team believes this strategy could work especially well along the regional borders of the python invasion. An adult female regularly lays around 70 eggs at a time, so removing them from these sites could slow the spread of their offspring into new areas.

The findings also pointed to a possibly unexpected conclusion. Florida runs its annual python hunting challenge in the summer, but organizers may want to consider rescheduling it during the winter. Data indicates that although fewer pythons are removed in months like January or February, their WRI ratings are much higher because they are mostly adults.
why_it_matters: Targeting the snakes that matter most could help protect Florida's native wildlife with less effort.

keywords.explanation: A kind of animal or plant that is not native to a place and can harm the local environment.
An approach with no rules about which targets to choose.
A scientist who studies how living things and their environment connect.
A new scoring system that gives more points to snakes whose removal helps most.
Fully grown and able to have babies.

questions.question: Why are Burmese pythons a problem in Florida?
options: They are an invasive species that can harm the local environment
They are a fish that eats farm crops in rivers
They are a native species that is quickly disappearing
They are a type of snake kept only in zoos
questions.correct_answer: They are an invasive species that can harm the local environment

questions.question: What is the Weighted Removal Index?
options: A prize chart for the winners of the hunting contest
A list of the names of every snake caught in Florida
A scoring system based on a snake's age, sex and the time of year
A map showing where hunters can drive their boats
questions.correct_answer: A scoring system based on a snake's age, sex and the time of year

questions.question: Which pythons does the index score highest?
options: Tiny young snakes
Snakes found only in summer
Mature female pythons
Male snakes of every size

questions.question: Why do young snakes get a lower score?
options: They are too small to be seen by hunters
Many die naturally before they can breed
They are protected by a state law
They lay many eggs every winter
questions.correct_answer: Many die naturally before they can breed

questions.question: About how many eggs does an adult female regularly lay at a time?
options: Around 70
Around 10
Around 100
Around five

questions.question: What change might organizers of the hunting challenge consider?
options: Making it last for a whole year
Holding it twice every summer
Ending it and hunting only by night
Holding it in the winter instead of the summer
questions.correct_answer: Holding it in the winter instead of the summer

background_read: Florida's Everglades is a large wetland where invasive pythons live.
A native species is one that belongs naturally in a place; an invasive species is brought from somewhere else.
